# kernellib

> Kernels and scalable kernel methods for JAX, built on gaussx. Kernels are Equinox modules whose hyperparameters are array leaves; every Gram matrix becomes a gaussx linear operator (dense, structured or matrix-free), so solves, log-determinants and preconditioners come from gaussx. On top sit spectral densities and feature maps (random Fourier, orthogonal, FastFood, Nyström, Hilbert-space), kernel ridge regression at scale (KRR, Falkon, EigenPro), dependence measures (HSIC, CKA, MMD, distance correlation, permutation tests), graphs, graph kernels and kernel eigenmaps, and optional scikit-learn adapters. Use these instead of hand-writing distance matrices, Cholesky solves of K + σ²I, random features or HSIC estimators.

One package, `kernellib` (import `kernellib as kl`), installed from GitHub: `uv add "kernellib @ git+https://github.com/jejjohnson/kernellib.git"`; extras `[sklearn]` (the `kernellib.sklearn` adapters) and `[neighbors]` (approximate nearest neighbours). Priors and GP models live in pyrox-gp, which wraps these kernels. Before writing a helper, search the capability index — every public name with a one-line summary, plus gaussx and geonnax. Code you add should keep three rules:

- **Hyperparameters are leaves:** build kernels with array hyperparameters (`kl.RBF(lengthscale=ell)`) and rebuild rather than mutate them, so `jax.grad` reaches them through fits.
- **Solves through gaussx:** `gaussx.solve(kl.to_operator(kernel, X, noise=s2), y)`, never `cho_solve` on a Gram; `implicit=True` and an iterative strategy (or `kl.KRR(preconditioner=...)`) for large N.
- **Fits return new objects, randomness takes keys:** `KRR(...).fit(X, y)` and `RandomFourierFeatures(R, key).fit(kernel, X)` return fitted copies; every random routine takes an explicit key.

Claude Code users can install the `kernellib` plugin: `/plugin marketplace add jejjohnson/kernellib`, then `/plugin install kernellib@kernellib`.

## Start here

- [Home](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/): what kernellib owns, how it sits on gaussx and geonnax
- [Architecture](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/architecture/): the layers, the kernel / operator / feature-map / estimator contracts
- [Capability index](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/reference/capabilities/): every public name, grouped by module, with a summary; then gaussx and geonnax
- [Building with agents](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/agents/): the Claude Code plugin, this file, and rules to paste into your project's AGENTS.md
- [Kernels and JAX](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/kernels-and-jax/): derivatives, gradients and transforms through kernels

## API reference

- [Overview](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/reference/)
- [Kernels](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/reference/kernels/): kernel classes, composition, derivative kernels, `to_operator`
- [Functional](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/reference/functional/): kernels and statistics as pure functions on arrays
- [Operators](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/reference/operators/): dense, implicit and low-rank kernel operators
- [Spectral](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/reference/spectral/): spectral densities, random-feature and Nyström maps, landmarks
- [Heuristics](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/reference/heuristics/): lengthscale estimates and grids
- [Regression](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/reference/regression/): KRR, Falkon, EigenPro
- [Dependence](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/reference/dependence/): HSIC, CKA, MMD, distance correlation, permutation tests
- [Graphs](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/reference/graph/): graph builders, Laplacians, graph kernels
- [Decomposition](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/reference/decomposition/): kernel PCA, eigenmaps, projections
- [scikit-learn](https://jejjohnson.github.io/kernellib/reference/sklearn/): the optional adapters
